instructions:
Read the paper below and produce a structured summary.

It matched these tracked topics; `relevance` must contain one entry per slug, stating what this paper changes for that topic:
- overthinking: Overthinking — When and why large reasoning models think more than a problem needs (or less than it needs) — the accuracy/efficiency tradeoff of reasoning length, test-time compute scaling, and methods to make a model stop, or keep going, at the right point.

Rules:
- Write in en.
- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.
- No marketing language. Prefer the specific number over the adjective.
- Return one JSON object matching the schema exactly. No prose around it.

concepts: string - reusable ideas this paper relies on or introduces

payload.title: Certain Head, Uncertain Tail: Expert-Sample for Test-Time Scaling in Fine-Grained MoE

contributions: Observes that in fine-grained MoE routers, expert scores split into a high-confidence 'head' and an uncertain 'tail'.
Proposes Expert-Sample, a training-free test-time scaling method that keeps head expert selections greedy while injecting controlled randomness only into tail expert routing.
Shows this avoids the diversity-stability tradeoff that token-level temperature sampling incurs, while keeping normal-temperature decoding.
Reports gains in pass@32 and Best-of-N verified accuracy on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct.
result.method: In fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts models, router scores over experts show a confident head and an uncertain tail. Expert-Sample exploits this at inference time: it leaves the routing of high-confidence ('head') experts unchanged (greedy), and introduces controlled randomness only in the selection among low-confidence ('tail') experts. This produces diverse generations for test-time scaling (e.g. multiple sampled solutions for pass@k or Best-of-N) without perturbing token-level sampling temperature, which the paper argues avoids the usual tradeoff between output diversity and stability.
result.one_liner: Expert-Sample scales test-time compute for fine-grained MoE LLMs by randomizing only low-confidence expert routing choices, keeping high-confidence expert selections fixed, to get diverse samples without the usual diversity-stability tradeoff of temperature sampling.
result.problem: Token-level temperature sampling used to generate diverse candidates for test-time scaling (e.g. pass@k, Best-of-N) trades off diversity against stability; the paper asks whether MoE routing structure offers a better axis for controlling diversity at inference time.

relevance.overthinking: Directly relevant: it is a test-time compute scaling method for reasoning-capable MoE LLMs, improving the accuracy/efficiency return of sampling more candidates at inference (pass@k, Best-of-N verification) by changing where randomness is injected, rather than lengthening or shortening a single reasoning chain.

result.results: On Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct with GPQA-Diamond, pass@32 improved from 85.4% to 91.9%, and Best-of-N verified accuracy improved from 59.1% to 62.6%.
